country.comment: Study examines municipal water supply and sewerage provision across Colombian municipalities from 2008 to 2019.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Resumen; PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Introducción

effect_estimate.comment: Dependent variables in Tables 6 and 7 are normalized log-transformed municipal coverage rates; standard errors are reported in parentheses rather than 95% CIs. Descriptive coverage from 2008 to 2019 rose in urban areas (aqueduct 79.2% to 89.2%; sewerage 71.8% to 80.8%) but stagnated in rural areas (aqueduct 34.5% to 37.1%; sewerage 12.6% to 13.2%).
effect_estimate.value: Hausman-Taylor panel regressions (2008-2019, 3 mayoral periods) on normalized log-transformed municipal coverage rates show: (1) Fiscal decentralization: earmarked national SGP water transfers (Lnsgpagua) positively affect urban aqueduct coverage (all municipalities: beta = 1.188, SE = 0.462, p < 0.05, N = 1,747 obs/802 municipalities; small municipalities: beta = 1.173, SE = 0.478, p < 0.05, N = 1,662 obs/765 municipalities) but have no statistically significant effect on rural aqueduct coverage (all: beta = -0.131, SE = 0.423) or on urban or rural sewerage coverage (urban all: beta = 0.136, SE = 0.367; rural all: beta = -0.280, SE = 0.429). Own-source property tax revenue (Lnpredia) increases urban aqueduct coverage (all: beta = 0.429, SE = 0.153, p < 0.01; small: beta = 0.365, SE = 0.157, p < 0.05; large/medium: beta = 2.189, SE = 0.877, p < 0.05) and urban sewerage coverage (all: beta = 0.516, SE = 0.140, p < 0.01; small: beta = 0.442, SE = 0.142, p < 0.01; large/medium: beta = 1.129, SE = 0.459, p < 0.05), while total municipal tax revenue (Lntribut) increases rural aqueduct coverage (all: beta = 0.433, SE = 0.153, p < 0.01; small: beta = 0.373, SE = 0.158, p < 0.05) and rural sewerage coverage (all: beta = 0.426, SE = 0.180, p < 0.05; small: beta = 0.411, SE = 0.191, p < 0.05). Royalties (Lnregal) positively affect urban aqueduct coverage in small municipalities (beta = 0.0873, SE = 0.0335, p < 0.01) but negatively affect rural aqueduct (all: beta = -0.0650, SE = 0.0307, p < 0.05) and large/medium municipal coverage. (2) Political dimension: party competition (enp, sumrank2) has no robust significant effect on any outcome; voter turnout (Lnturnout) is negatively associated with rural sewerage coverage in all municipalities (beta = -1.640, SE = 0.800, p < 0.05, N = 1,631 obs/767 municipalities) and small municipalities (beta = -1.832, SE = 0.827, p < 0.05) and marginally positive in large/medium municipalities (beta = 10.01, SE = 5.340, p < 0.10). (3) Administrative capacity & metropolitan coordination: the municipal management index (Lnmdm_ges) shows mixed effects—negative in urban areas (aqueduct all: beta = -7.253, SE = 2.519, p < 0.01; sewerage all: beta = -6.079, SE = 1.781, p < 0.01) and positive in rural areas (aqueduct all: beta = 6.578, SE = 2.130, p < 0.01; sewerage all: beta = 5.521, SE = 1.886, p < 0.01). Belonging to a Functional Urban Area (Dummy AUF) reduces urban aqueduct coverage (all: beta = -2.338, SE = 0.908, p < 0.05; small: beta = -1.775, SE = 0.737, p < 0.05) as well as urban sewerage (small: beta = -1.500, SE = 0.567, p < 0.01) and rural sewerage coverage (small: beta = -1.035, SE = 0.605, p < 0.10).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Appraised with ROBINS-I, the study has Serious risk of bias (backward imputation of 2016-2019 MDM administrative scores to 2008-2015, iterative data-driven classification of endogenous vs. exogenous regressors, reliance solely on internal panel instruments, and no external shock/unexposed comparator), so the design ceiling caps certainty below 3. Because the regressions capture municipal-level statistical associations while specific administrative/legal mechanisms (e.g., planning hurdles, procedural steps, lack of inter-municipal metropolitan coordination, uniform regulatory requirements on rural community aqueducts) are interpreted from secondary reports rather than directly observed in primary process data, certainty is 1.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines political participation/electoral turnout (participation), municipal management including territorial ordering plans (planning), lack of inter-municipal/metropolitan cooperation in Functional Urban Areas and regional water markets (political_coordination), multiplicity of sectoral/environmental/territorial authorities and plans plus multiple administrative procedures/instances faced by mayors (institutional_fragmentation, procedural_steps), and need for flexible legal/regulatory provision schemes suited to rural and community aqueducts under Law 142 of 1994 (accommodation).

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Quantitative longitudinal panel econometric study using the Hausman-Taylor instrumental-variables panel estimator (combining fixed-effects and random-effects internal instruments with Sargan-Hansen overidentification tests) to estimate causal effects of fiscal, political, and administrative decentralization dimensions following Colombia's 2008 SGP transfer reform; fits ROBINS-I as a panel IV/FE policy evaluation design (with Serious overall risk of bias due to backward-imputed 2016-2019 administrative index values and data-driven regressor exogeneity selection).

sample_size.comment: Spatial delimitation covers 1,103 Colombian municipalities across 5 natural regions; descriptive panel tables contain up to 2,907 municipality-period observations (2,878 for coverage) across three 4-year mayoral terms (2008-2011, 2012-2015, 2016-2019), and Hausman-Taylor regression models include up to 893 municipalities (2,188 observations) for aqueduct and 877 municipalities (2,179 observations) for sewerage.
sample_size.value: 1,103 municipalities delimited nationally; panel dataset of up to 2,907 municipality-period observations (2,878 coverage observations) across 3 four-year mayoral periods (2008-2011, 2012-2015, 2016-2019); econometric estimation samples of 802 to 893 municipalities (1,747 to 2,188 municipality-period observations) for aqueduct coverage and 767 to 877 municipalities (1,631 to 2,179 municipality-period observations) for sewerage coverage

study_design.comment: Municipal-level longitudinal panel data study (3 four-year mayoral government periods: 2008-2011, 2012-2015, 2016-2019) using the Hausman-Taylor instrumental-variables panel estimator (with Breusch-Pagan, Hausman, and Sargan-Hansen post-estimation tests) to address endogeneity while estimating time-varying and time-invariant regressors.
study_design.value: Observational municipal panel econometric study applying the Hausman-Taylor instrumental-variables panel estimator across three four-year mayoral periods (2008-2019)
